hints: At bit b, zeros and ones alternate in blocks of length 2^b.
Count full cycles among 0 through n, then the remaining ones.
analogy: Each bit follows a repeating schedule: off for a block, then on for an equally long block.
example: From 1 through 3, binary values 1,10,11 contain 1+1+2=4 one bits.
algorithm: For each bit b with 2^b <= n, let h=2^b and N=n+1. Add floor(N/(2h))*h + max(0,N%(2h)-h). Print the sum using a wide integer.
correctness: Among numbers 0 through n, bit b has exactly h ones in each full cycle of length 2h, followed by the counted suffix of the partial cycle. Summing the independent bit counts counts every one bit once.
complexity: For n, O(log n) time and O(1) space.
